narrative.intro: Csi Aviation has $1.1B in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Csi Aviation won 9 awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $128M, and obligations are up 73.7% year over year. Csi Aviation received obligations from a small set of agencies: the Department of Homeland Security accounts for $1.1B, the Department of Defense accounts for $1.7M, and the Department of Energy accounts for $721K. Csi Aviation’s obligations are concentrated in travel and air-transport markets: All Other Travel Arrangement and Reservation Services accounts for $1.1B, and Nonscheduled Chartered Passenger Air Transportation accounts for $2.3M. Csi Aviation’s fiscal-year history shows growth in contract obligations: FY21 was $2.4M, FY22 was $4.8M, FY23 was $162M, FY24 was $350M, FY25 was $661M, and FY26 is $1.1B. Csi Aviation’s current-year totals are fiscal year to date and are contract obligations except where award-value labeling differs in award tables. This summary focuses on obligations and buyer concentration so contracting officers and capture teams can see where the business is strongest.

sections.heading: Why did obligations rise in FY2026?
sections.body: Csi Aviation’s FY2026 obligations reached $1.1B, up 73.7% year over year. Csi Aviation shows a step change from FY25 obligations of $661M to FY26 obligations of $1.1B, reflecting larger or more numerous awards in the current fiscal year. Csi Aviation’s average award size of $128M and award count of 9 indicate a concentration in relatively large awards. Csi Aviation’s buyer concentration with the Department of Homeland Security at $1.1B helps explain most of the increase.

sections.heading: Where are Csi Aviation’s obligations concentrated?
sections.body: Csi Aviation’s largest buying agency is the Department of Homeland Security with $1.1B in obligations. Csi Aviation’s top NAICS market is All Other Travel Arrangement and Reservation Services with $1.1B in obligations. Csi Aviation has much smaller obligations with the Department of Defense at $1.7M and the Department of Energy at $721K, and a secondary market in Nonscheduled Chartered Passenger Air Transportation at $2.3M.

faq.q: How much does Csi Aviation make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Csi Aviation has $1.1B in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Csi Aviation’s fiscal-year obligations grew from $661M in FY25 to $1.1B in FY26, and the company has 9 awards this fiscal year with an average award size of $128M.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Csi Aviation?
faq.a: The Department of Homeland Security buys the most from Csi Aviation, with $1.1B in obligations. The Department of Defense has $1.7M in obligations and the Department of Energy has $721K in obligations.

faq.q: What does Csi Aviation sell to the government?
faq.a: Csi Aviation sells travel and passenger air services to the government. Csi Aviation’s top NAICS market is All Other Travel Arrangement and Reservation Services with $1.1B in obligations, and Csi Aviation also provides Nonscheduled Chartered Passenger Air Transportation with $2.3M in obligations.
